loconautics.configuration.title: Create: Loconautics Config
loconautics.configuration.foundation.ena: Allows stations to assemble Loconautics physics trains.
Allows stations to assemble standard Create trains.
loconautics.configuration.train.bearingA: Top speed at 256 RPM with the Bearing Axle in gear 0. -1 = use Create's train top speed.
loconautics.configuration.train.trainMax: Hard ceiling on any train's speed, overdrive included. -1 = only the physics safety ceiling of 200.
A redstone signal into the top of a Bearing Axle shifts it into an overdrive gear. Off, every axle stays in gear 0.
How much top speed each spare SU buys in the highest gear. Higher lets a small network go faster.
Keeps every gear under Create's train top speed. Gears then only reach it at a lower RPM.
loconautics.configuration.train.maxBogey: Maximum Create bogeys allowed in one carriage (glued cluster). Default 2, matching Create.
Extra horizontal distance in blocks to scan beyond the station's assembly area.
How many blocks above the bogeys the station scans during assembly.
How many blocks below the bogeys the station scans during assembly.
Keeps chunks loaded around physics trains stopped at stations.
loconautics.configuration.train.dynamics: A train of this mass uses the base acceleration. Lighter trains accelerate faster and heavier ones more slowly.
Acceleration for a train at the reference mass.
Controls how strongly train mass affects acceleration. At 0, acceleration is independent of mass. At 1, it scales inversely with mass.
Floor under the weight scaled acceleration, so the heaviest rake still pulls away.
Ceiling over the weight scaled acceleration, so a near empty cart does not launch.
How quickly the brakes slow a train, regardless of its mass.
Acceleration multiplier when two seated drivers of one consist push the same way. Top speed does not change.
Acceleration multiplier when three or more seated drivers of one consist push the same way.
Controls how quickly a coasting train slows down. Set to 0 to disable rolling resistance.
Adds stress to working Bearing Axles when the train climbs a slope.
Extra stress impact per degree of climb, shared by the working axles.
loconautics.configuration.train.visual.b: Controls how strongly bogeys shift sideways in curves as train speed increases. Set to 0 to disable sway.
Caps the sideways offset from bogey sway.
Lets bogeys use physics pivots to follow the rails.
loconautics.configuration.train.relocati: Allows players to move physics trains with a Wrench.
Limits Wrench relocation to trains that have derailed.
loconautics.configuration.track.railSear: Horizontal search radius in blocks when looking for nearby track.
Vertical search range in blocks when looking for nearby track.
loconautics.configuration.track.railHopM: Maximum angle in degrees between the train's heading and a rail it can hop onto.
loconautics.configuration.track.derailme: Maximum angle in degrees that a rail can tilt away from level before a train derails.
Allows a strong upward push, such as from a Physics Staff, to lift a train off the rails.
Allows trains to derail when they hit the end of the track.
Impact threshold for derailment when a train hits the end of the track.
Scales the drive force of a derailed train on the ground. Set to 0 to disable this movement.
How much a collision must change a carriage's speed, in blocks per second, to derail it.
Allows coupled carriages in the same train to derail each other when they collide.
loconautics.configuration.track.rerail.a: Allows trains and off-track bogeys to return to nearby rails automatically.
Maximum speed at which a train can begin rerailing automatically.
loconautics.configuration.hatch.injector: Water storage capacity of fluid hatches and supported Hullsteel sockets, in millibuckets.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.bearing: Divides the mass assigned to each axle when calculating its stress impact per RPM. Lower values increase the impact.
Minimum stress impact even on an empty train.
Stress multiplier for a Bearing Axle driving against the rest of its train.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.analog_: Ticks between steps toward zero throttle when the controller is unattended, unlocked and free of schedule control.
Limits the reverse throttle signal when driving with the Analog Controller.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.transmi: Stress Units used by a Transmission per RPM of output speed.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.turntab: Stress Units used by a Turntable Bearing per RPM of plate speed.
loconautics.configuration.items.steel_ca: Maximum distance in blocks between two ends of a Steel Cable.
loconautics.configuration.couplers.knuck: Ticks between scans for new knuckle coupler connections.
loconautics.configuration.couplers.twist: How hard a coupler resists two Carriages leaning apart, as a share of the lighter one's wheel hinge. 0 turns it off.
Free twist in a coupler before it starts passing lean to the next Carriage.
loconautics.configuration.hose.maxLength: Maximum length in blocks for a hose connection.
loconautics.configuration.explosions.sub: Allows explosions to push nearby Sable contraptions.
Scales the knockback radius based on the explosion's power.
Scales how strongly an explosion pushes nearby contraptions.
Adds an upward component to the explosion's knockback.
Minimum distance in blocks used in the inverse-square knockback calculation.
loconautics.configuration.explosions.dem: Base explosion power setting for Demolition Charges.
Configured limit on the number of charges.
Configured fuse delay in game ticks.
loconautics.configuration.compat.compute: Allows computers to control trains, signals, points and turntables by ID. Turning this off limits control to computers inside the train.
loconautics.configuration.patch.enableRo: Allows Mechanical Rollers to work on moving Sable contraptions.
loconautics.configuration.patch.enablePl: Allows Mechanical Ploughs to work on moving Sable contraptions.
loconautics.configuration.patch.rollerHe: How many blocks above the surface a Mechanical Roller clears.
loconautics.configuration.patch.requireM: Controls whether the Create patches should consume materials for block placement.
loconautics.configuration.gauges.dialWob: Needle wobble in degrees on gauges. Set to 0 to keep the needle steady.

loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_1: A Hose Nozzle turns into its own physics body the moment it is placed. It falls, swings and is pushed around like any loose object
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_2: Click the winch with a Hose, then the nozzle, in either order. A dotted line previews the run while one end is selected
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_3: The preview goes orange while you are pointing at something that is not the other end, and red once you are past twenty eight blocks. Sneak click to drop the selection
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_4: Hose stretches a little past what has been paid out. Once it is that taut the winch can only give more out, it cannot haul against it
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_1: A Mechanical Pump on the face opposite the one the winch is bolted to is what pressurizes the line. No pump, no flow, however full the tank is
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_2: Pump speed sets how far the pressure reaches, up to twenty eight blocks at Create's top rpm. A hose longer than that reach delivers nothing
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_3: Docked, everything the pump sends goes into the hatch's tank, and it can draw back the other way too
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_4: Loose, it sprays instead, and the jet kicks back hard enough to shove the nozzle around
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_1: Right click it with an empty hand to take hold, and again to let go. Scroll to push it further out or pull it closer, and hold Tab while moving the mouse to turn it
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_2: Bring it near a Fluid Hatch and it docks itself, upright and locked to the socket. It does not have to be held for that
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_3: Grabbing a docked nozzle pops it straight back out of the socket. Driving away does the same on its own once the hose goes taut, which is what saves a hose left plugged in
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_1: Water puts fires out, soaks farmland to full and takes the burning off anything caught in the jet
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_2: Lava does the opposite, lighting whatever surface the jet lands on and setting mobs alight
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_3: Potions carry their own effects to anyone sprayed, and honey bogs them down. The jet is colored from the fluid it is throwing
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_4: Any other fluid is fair game. A datapack binds it to one of the named effects, or an addon registers its own
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_1: A Hose Winch bolts flat against whatever face you click. Its reel axle always lies horizontal, whichever way it is mounted
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_2: Rotation is the reel. One way pays hose out, the other hauls it back, and faster rotation moves it faster
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_3: A redstone signal puts the reel in free spin. Pulling the hose out spins the winch and generates up to 256 su, and the faster the hose moves the faster it turns
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_4: Break the winch and the hose snaps, popping the Hose item back out where the winch stood. The winch owns the hose, the nozzle only holds the far end
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_1: Bind a control to a Redstone Link receiver first. It has to be a receiver, a transmitter is not something a panel can drive
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_2: A button sends a full signal for one second
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_3: A switch is the same signal, held. It stays where you left it
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_4: A lever is analog. Hold the click and drag to sweep it anywhere from zero to fifteen
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_5: Two controls on one link do not fight. The strongest one wins, and the link falls back when it lets go
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_1: Gauges, valves, buttons, levers and switches all live in the same block, a panel with four quadrants
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_2: Aim at a free quadrant and the next part lands there. Aim at the middle of a bare face and the first part sits centered instead, until a second one moves it into a corner
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_3: A wrench configures whichever part you are pointing at, and every part carries its own body and color choices
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_4: Sneak with the wrench to take one part back. Breaking the panel with parts still in it takes them one at a time, the block only goes when the last one leaves
